_comment: Encoded design factors: what a descriptor value implies for making. Edit here, not in code.
_status: PROVISIONAL. Drawn from Study 1 site experience and general handling/fabrication practice. Not verified with domain experts. Every derived output carries data_status 'proposed'.
_circularity_note: Thresholds were informed by Study 1. Agreement between derived outputs and Study 1 decisions is therefore expected and is NOT validation.

use_suggestions.basis: Study 1 programme: landscape installation and urban furniture. Fragments serve as supports, stands, shelves, seats and worktops within an assembly. Ground surfacing and downcycling to fill or aggregate are out of scope by design.
use_suggestions._how_to_read: Each entry combines conditions on one face with conditions on the whole fragment. A suggestion is offered when the fragment satisfies requires_fragment and at least one face satisfies requires_face; requires_no_face fires when no face qualifies. Thickness = smallest bounding dimension; aspect ratio = longest / smallest; height_band_mm matches if ANY bounding dimension falls in the band, since the fragment can be laid to present that dimension as height. Which orientation is stable is not computed.

rules.label: Bench or table top
rules.note: flat, smooth cast face large enough to sit at or place objects on; thick enough to span

rules.label: Leaning or backrest surface
rules.note: large face, mass resists displacement. Resting-pose orientation is not computed, so the angle the face presents once placed is unverified

rules.label: Exposed face, material history visible
rules.note: carries visible traces of the fragment's former life; candidate to face outward

rules.label: Textured feature surface
rules.note: deliberately rough face, exposing the break and aggregate as visible and tactile character

rules.label: Cut to create a bearing face
rules.note: substantial fragment with no usable flat face; a wall or wire saw could create one

rules.label: Planter or void reuse
rules.note: a former pipe or conduit penetration, detected in the texture, can be reinterpreted as a planting pocket or light opening, as in Study 1
rules.caveat: opening detected from the image only; depth and whether it passes through are not measured

rules.label: Seat or stool
rules.note: presents a sittable height with a flat enough top face; heavy enough to stay put

rules.label: Bar-table or high-table stand
rules.note: stands at counter height with a bearing face on top to carry a table plate

rules.label: Low support or side table
rules.note: low bearing element: side table, footrest, or plinth beneath a larger piece

rules.label: Pedestal or structural support
rules.note: broad flat bearing face and mass enough to carry a timber deck, plate or slab above

rules.label: Shelf or spanning slab
rules.note: slab-like and elongated with a flat face; spans between two supports as a shelf or seat plate
